def: A horizontal lane in the Tracks area where you record, play back and edit regions. Each track plays through its own channel strip in the Mixer.

def: A block on a track that holds a piece of your recording. Audio regions point to part of an audio file; MIDI regions hold notes. You build a song by moving, copying and editing regions.

def: The main part of the Logic window, where your tracks and their regions sit.

def: The vertical line that shows where playback is. Drag it to hear a different point in the song.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: The on-screen version of a strip on a mixing desk: a volume fader, a pan knob, a Mute button, and slots for inputs, outputs, sends and effects. Your tracks' sound runs through their channel strips.

def: The window that shows every track's channel strip side by side, so you can balance levels and set up effects. Press X to show or hide it.

def: Musical Instrument Digital Interface. MIDI is note information — which pitch, how long, how loud — sent between keyboards, computers and instruments. It is not sound itself; an instrument turns it into sound.

def: Recorded sound — a voice, a guitar, anything captured through a microphone or input — stored in audio files and placed on audio tracks as audio regions.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: An instrument that runs inside Logic — a synthesizer, a sampler or a re-creation of a vintage instrument — played with MIDI from a keyboard or from MIDI regions.

def: An add-on that gives a track its sound or changes it — usually a software instrument or an effect.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: A ready-made sound you load onto a track. It can include the instrument, its effects and other channel strip settings.

def: A set of on-screen knobs for shaping the selected track's sound — usually tone and EQ, reverb and other effects — without opening each plug-in. Press B to show them.

def: A panel that shows settings for whatever is selected. The Region inspector, for example, shows the playback settings of the selected regions.

def: Recorded or drawn changes to a control over time — a fader rising, a filter opening — that Logic plays back for you. Volume, pan, sends and most plug-in settings can be automated.

def: A route that carries sound from a send to an aux channel strip, where it can be processed or mixed with other tracks.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: A control on a channel strip that routes its sound along a bus to an aux channel strip. Choose a bus in a Send slot and Logic creates the aux for you.

def: An aux (auxiliary) channel strip receives sound sent to it over a bus, so it can be processed or combined into a submix.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: A delay between a sound going in and you hearing it come out. Processing takes time, so plug-ins and the audio buffer both add latency — which you notice most while recording.

def: The chunk of audio your Mac processes at a time. A smaller I/O buffer means less latency but more strain on the processor; too small for your Mac and you hear clicks, pops and crackles.

src.label: Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

def: The speed of the music in beats per minute (bpm). At 120 bpm there are 120 beats every minute.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: Moving notes so they start exactly on the nearest point of a timing grid, tightening up playing that is slightly early or late.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

def: Makes edits land on the nearest grid position — a bar, a beat or a finer division — so things stay in time. Turn it on or off with the button next to the Snap menu.

def: How hard a note was played, from 0 to 127. It usually sets the note's loudness, and can shape other parts of the sound too.

def: A tool that selects a range of time instead of whole regions. Drag across one or more tracks and only the part inside is selected, ready to move, cut, copy or delete.

def: Logic's built-in virtual musicians. Drummer was joined by Bass Player and Keyboard Player in Logic Pro 11, and by Synth Player in Logic Pro 12. Bass Player and Keyboard Player can follow your chord progression.
